contest: Most red members at round end (a member that counts as several counts that many).

story.line: Red recruits: free members, and swaps with the shop and with rivals' members.
story.greatGame: Round I: take Gather or Walk-In, and pick up cheap red bodies (Seat Filler, Foster Parents, Loyalists, Deprogrammers) so you lead the red members contest early. Round II: Seat Filler trades up at round start, Promote takes a rival's best member for one of yours, and every member that arrives from a rival pays Foster Parents. Round III: Initiation takes a 10-cost member free, and Patriarch pays for the wide cult at game end. Rivals answer by buying Loyalists themselves, taking Initiation first, or swapping your engine pieces away with your own Promote and Demote.
freshStart: Space, round I: "Open Call: Recruit a shop member costing 4 or less, for free. +1 red."
Space, round II: "Trade Up: Give one of your members to the shop and recruit a shop member costing up to 4 more, for free. +2 red."
Space, round III: "Mass Initiation: Recruit two shop members costing 5 or less each, for free."
Member: "Barkers: On Use, once per round: recruit a shop member costing 3 or less, for free."
Member: "Recruiting Sergeant: Whenever you recruit a red member, +1 follower."
Member: "Defectors: Whenever one of your members goes to a rival's cult, recruit a shop member costing 4 or less, for free."

cards.name: Tryout
cards.text: Use the On Recruit effect of a shop member; it stays in the shop. +2 red.
cards.bestTurn: Round III, the shop shows Mentor ("On Recruit: recruit the cheapest member in the shop."). I use Mentor's On Recruit: a 5-cost member joins free, plus 2 red. About 7, against Gather's 4 red and 3 followers (7).
cards.topCase: Round III, used every chance: it is only as good as the best On Recruit in the shop, about 5 to 7. Never breaks the game; some rounds the shop has nothing worth using and it is 2 red.
cards.ideaWhy: Try a member's welcome without hiring it; but using another card's effect is Green's copying verb.
cards.ties: Makes the shop's On Recruit members matter to everyone, and sits beside Green's Sample, which does the same with a rival's member.
cards.coryNotes: His idea (Oct 27, yes 12:23pm). Nov 1: "1 yes" to +2 red.
cards.why: A good small turn when the shop cooperates, flat when it doesn't, and it borrows Green's job.
cards.short: Round III: use Mentor's On Recruit, a 5-cost member free, plus 2 red.
cards.risk: Overlaps Green's Sample: using another member's On Recruit.

cards.name: Gather
cards.text: +2 red in round I, +3 in round II, +4 in round III. This turn, if you recruit a member, +1 follower in round I, +2 in round II, +3 in round III.
cards.bestTurn: Round I: +2 red, then I recruit a 5-cost Foster Parents and get +1 follower. Gain over Walk-In is small; it is the safe fuel turn.
cards.topCase: Round III, recruiting every time: +4 red and +3 followers, about 7, against Initiation's free 10-cost member. Never breaks the game.
cards.ideaWhy: Fuel that pays you for recruiting, the color's verb.
cards.ties: Feeds red held toward pricier members; same shape as Magenta's Stash and White's Allowance.
cards.coryNotes: Oct 31, "B" (this version). Oct 31: "default to gather style for now for the rest".
cards.why: Does its job as the fuel space; no moment anyone retells, and three colors now have the same card.
cards.short: Round III: +4 red, and +3 followers if you recruit that turn.
cards.risk: Same card as Magenta's Stash and White's Allowance.

cards.name: Walk-In
cards.text: Recruit the top member of the pile. Each rival +1 red. +1 red.
cards.bestTurn: Round I: I flip Loyalists (worth 3, counts as 3) and take it free, +1 red; each rival gets 1 red. A 5-cost member for one minion, against Gather's 2 red.
cards.topCase: Round III, the pile holds round III members: a blind free member, usually 8 to 10 cost, sometimes a 14-cost Mob. A second, uncapped Initiation by luck; strong but not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: Take whoever walks in the door; the red to rivals is the price.
cards.ties: Gives every rival red, which helps them buy and does nothing for the red members contest; pulls from the pile, so it changes what the shop will deal.
cards.coryNotes: His words, Oct 27 12:53pm: "Recruit the top member of the deck. Each rival +1 red."
cards.why: A free member in round I is a real turn; in round III it crowds Initiation's moment with a blind version of it.
cards.short: Round III: flip the pile's top member, often 8 to 10 cost, free.
cards.risk: Overlaps Initiation: a blind, uncapped free member in round III.

cards.name: Promote
cards.text: Swap any member with one in another cult or the shop costing up to 3 more. +3 red.
cards.bestTurn: Round II: I give my 5-cost Seat Filler to a rival and take their 8-cost Recruiter, +3 red. I gain 3 cost of member and their red income is now mine; they feel it at once.
cards.topCase: Round III: swap my 7-cost Host for a rival's 10-cost Patriarch: +3 red, I gain Patriarch's game end, they lose it. About 6 to 9 of swing. Strong, not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: Trade up, from anyone; the color's own swap.
cards.ties: Moves members between cults, so it pays Foster Parents and Deprogrammers and is what Loyalists exists to stop.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 5: "i like it better as any… do you understand the intent of promote or demote?"
cards.why: The swap that makes Red Red, with a sting a rival feels; he defended it, but the same turn sits beside it as Demote.
cards.short: Round III: swap your 7-cost Host for a rival's 10-cost Patriarch, +3 red.
cards.risk: Overlaps Demote and Seat Filler: the same swap.

cards.name: Demote
cards.text: Swap any member with one in another cult or the shop costing up to 3 less. +3 red.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: the leader's 14-cost Mob goes to the shop, and an 11-cost shop member goes to them; +3 red. They lose Mob's round end payout and 3 cost of member.
cards.topCase: Round III, aimed at the leader: strips their best engine piece for about 3 to 6 swing plus 3 red. Not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: A near twin of Promote at the same moment, the same swap read the other way.
cards.ties: Same as Promote: pays Foster Parents and Deprogrammers, blocked by Loyalists.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 5: "i like it better as any… do you understand the intent of promote or demote?"
cards.why: A real way to knock the leader down, but the one you'd miss sooner of the pair.
cards.short: Round III: send the leader's 14-cost Mob to the shop, +3 red.
cards.risk: Overlaps Promote and Headhunter: the same swap, pulling members out.

cards.name: Initiation
cards.text: Recruit a member in the shop costing 10 or less, for free. +1 red.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: I take Patriarch (10 cost, game end +1 follower per 2 members) free, +1 red. About 10 plus the card, against Spree's two extra recruits and 6 blue.
cards.topCase: Round III, once: about 10 to 12. Beside Poach (a rival's member of any cost, free) and Largesse (+10 followers) it sits level. Never breaks.
cards.ideaWhy: A free member, the color's verb at full size.
cards.ties: Takes the best card out of the shop before anyone else can buy it.
cards.coryNotes: Oct 13: Rally, Encore and Payroll "weren't strong enough"; he chose taking a member free. Oct 24: "8 or less" (now 10 with prices).
cards.why: His pick for this slot, and the cleanest big Red turn.
cards.short: Round III: take the 10-cost Patriarch from the shop free, +1 red.
cards.risk: Overlaps Walk-In: a blind, uncapped version in round III.

cards.name: Body Snatchers
cards.text: Round Start: swap one of your members with a rival's member of the same cost.
cards.bestTurn: Bought in round II, at round III start I swap my 8-cost Headhunter for a rival's 8-cost Recruiter. Same cost, so I gain only the better ability.
cards.topCase: It deals from round II, so it fires once, at round III start, and only if a rival holds a member at exactly the cost of one of mine. Pays about 2 to 3; flat.
cards.ideaWhy: Swap bodies at night; but the same-cost rule makes it rare.
cards.ties: Pays Foster Parents and stings with Deprogrammers when it fires; Loyalists stops it.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 5: maybe cheaper, "the cost being limiting makes it bad as well".
cards.why: One round start a game and an exact cost match: it often does nothing.
cards.short: Round III start: swap your 8-cost member for a rival's 8-cost one.

cards.name: Seat Filler
cards.text: Round Start: you may give this to the shop and recruit a shop member costing up to 3 more, for free.
cards.bestTurn: Round I I pay 5 for it; at round II start I trade it for an 8-cost Recruiter, free. A cheap buy that turns into the member I wanted.
cards.topCase: Fires once (it leaves when used): about +3 cost of member and a better ability. Never breaks.
cards.ideaWhy: A placeholder that trades up, Promote done by the card itself.
cards.ties: Puts a cheap member back in the shop for rivals and takes a better one off it.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 4: "I like Drifter." (its first name). Nov 5: "Swap out volunteer for Seat Filler".
cards.why: He liked it, and it gives round I a reason to buy cheap.
cards.short: Round II start: trade this 5-cost member for an 8-cost Recruiter, free.
cards.risk: Overlaps Promote: the same trade up.

cards.name: Mentor
cards.text: On Recruit: recruit the cheapest member in the shop.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: I pay 11 and the cheapest shop member, a 5-cost Foster Parents, comes along free. Two members, Recruiter and Proselytizers each pay twice.
cards.topCase: Round III only (it deals then): 11 paid for worth 1 plus a 4 to 6-cost member. Less than 11 followers bought outright. Flat; shines only when Tryout or Green copies it.
cards.ties: Empties the cheap end of the shop; a good card for Tryout and Green's Sample to borrow.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 5: counts as 1 member ("backlog yes"); kept Oct 18 as part of Red's upper ladder ("yep").
cards.why: The price buys less than the same resources spent on followers.
cards.short: Round III: pay 11, and a 5-cost member comes along free.

cards.name: Proselytizers
cards.bestTurn: Round III with Blue's Spree: three recruits in one turn, +3 followers on top.
cards.topCase: Deals in round III: about 4 to 6 recruits after buying it, so +4 to +6 plus worth 2, for 10. Fine, not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: Every new face brings a follower.
cards.ties: Rewards extra recruits from anywhere (Blue's Spree, Walk-In, Initiation, follower buys).
cards.coryNotes: Oct 30: "Loyalists and Proselytizer stay." Nov 4: Evangelists and Zealots "are no, those are going in the cut pile" (its replacements); Proselytizers stays.
cards.why: He kept it over two replacements; steady, never a moment.
cards.short: Round III: Blue's Spree makes three recruits, +3 followers on top.

cards.name: Mob
cards.text: Round End: +2 followers per rival with fewer red members than you.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: Mob alone is 4 red members, so at round end all three rivals have fewer: +6 followers.
cards.topCase: Deals in round III, so it pays one round end: +6 plus worth 4 = 10, for 14. Less than buying followers. Not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: It counts as 4 red members itself, so it meets its own condition; it reads as a flat +6.
cards.ties: Doubles up the red members contest Mob already decides by itself.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 3: "Mob is probably just too strong needs rework?" Current text is Claude's rework (Nov 4); no word from him since.
cards.why: Out-redding rivals is automatic once you own it, so nobody can fight it, and one payout doesn't cover the price.
cards.short: Round III end: 4 red members beats all three rivals, +6 followers.

cards.name: Recruiter
cards.text: Whenever you recruit a member, +1 red.
cards.bestTurn: As the Red cloak: a member every turn of round II, +4 red that round, enough for one extra member by round III.
cards.topCase: As a shop member it deals in round III: about 3 to 5 red, for 8. As the cloak all game: about 10 to 12 red. Not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: Each recruit pays toward the next.
cards.ties: Swaps and steals count too, so it pays off Promote and Initiation.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 1: "yeah version 1" (this text). Nov 3: "we need to nerf red a little"; it stayed as is.
cards.why: Good as the cloak; as a member bought in round III it barely pays back.
cards.short: As the Red cloak, recruit every turn: about 12 red over a game.
cards.risk: Overlaps Host: both are red income.

cards.name: Host
cards.text: On Recruit: +1 red per 2 members you have. Round Start: +1 red per 2 members you have.
cards.bestTurn: Round II with 6 members: +3 red now, then +4 at round III start.
cards.topCase: Two payouts at most, about 7 red, for 7. Flat.
cards.ideaWhy: A wide cult throws a party; plain income.
cards.ties: Same job as Recruiter, making red, counted a different way.
cards.coryNotes: Kept in an October cut ("Cory keeps Host…"); no words since.
cards.why: Pays back its price and nothing more; the member you'd miss least.
cards.short: Round II with 6 members: +3 red now, +4 at round III start.
cards.risk: Overlaps Recruiter: both are red income.

cards.name: Patriarch
cards.text: Game End: +1 follower per 2 members you have.
cards.bestTurn: Round III Red cult with Deprogrammers (4), Loyalists (3) and four others: 11 members, +5 at game end.
cards.topCase: Built around it: about 14 members counted, +7, plus worth 1, for 10. Fine, not breaking.
cards.ideaWhy: The color's go-deep card: the bigger the family, the more it pays.
cards.ties: Makes the members that count as several worth more again.
cards.coryNotes: Oct 24: "yes yes yes. go deep card for every color". Nov 4: "absolutely not" to Godfather, its replacement; Patriarch stays.
cards.why: He kept it over a replacement; a solid finish, no moment until the end.

cards.name: Foster Parents
cards.text: Whenever a member joins your cult from a rival’s, +2 followers.
cards.bestTurn: Round II: Promote takes a rival's Recruiter, +2; round III start Body Snatchers brings one more, +2.
cards.topCase: Bought in round I, about one rival member a round: +4 to +6 plus worth 2, for 6. Fine.
cards.ideaWhy: Taking in another cult's members pays.
cards.ties: Pays off Red's swaps and Magenta's steals; also pays a rival who trades for it.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 6: "increase the cost a tad", then "lower" (stays a round I member).
cards.why: Gives Red's swaps a payoff, but it does the same job as Deprogrammers.
cards.short: Each rival's member that joins you pays +2 followers, about +6 a game.
cards.risk: Overlaps Deprogrammers: both pay when you take a rival's member.

cards.name: Deprogrammers
cards.text: Whenever you take a rival’s member out of their cult, they lose 1 follower.
cards.bestTurn: Round I: 5 resources buys 4 red members, and that alone wins the red members contest, +4.
cards.topCase: The rule pays about 1 to 2 over a game; the card is really a cheap 4-member body that decides the contest. Strong for its price.
cards.ideaWhy: A big cheap body with a small sting added on; nobody plans around the -1.
cards.ties: Swings the red members contest and Patriarch more than its printed rule does anything.
cards.coryNotes: Oct 30: "come up with a better name".
cards.why: Its printed rule hardly matters; what decides games is the 4-member body for 5.
cards.short: Round I: 5 resources buys 4 red members and wins the red contest.
cards.risk: Cheap 4-member body decides the red contest; overlaps Foster Parents.

cards.name: Panel
cards.text: On Use, once per round: promote or demote another of your members.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: I trade my 6-cost Foster Parents for a rival's 9-cost member on my own turn without a minion.
cards.topCase: Deals in round III, so it is used once: one swap of about 3 cost, plus worth 3 and 3 red members, for 9. Fine.
cards.ideaWhy: Promote and Demote on a card.
cards.ties: Pays Foster Parents; Loyalists stops it.
cards.coryNotes: Nov 5: On Use, once per round ("backlog yes").
cards.why: A useful swap and a big body, but it repeats two spaces.
cards.short: Round III: swap your 6-cost Foster Parents for a rival's 9-cost member, no minion.
cards.risk: Overlaps Promote and Demote, on a member.

cards.name: Loyalists
cards.text: Your other members can’t be swapped.
cards.bestTurn: Round I, 5 resources: 3 red members, and in round II the rival on Promote finds my cult shut.
cards.topCase: A shield all game plus 3 red members for 5; rivals must swap Loyalists itself first. Strong for its price, not breaking.
cards.ties: Shuts off every swap card against you (Promote, Demote, Panel, Body Snatchers, Headhunter); not steals.
cards.coryNotes: Oct 27: "Loyalists are too strong… just have no counter and prevent member meddling, its frustrating when a player is ahead and takes it and protects their engine." Oct 30: stays. Nov 6: "yes" to 2 red + 2 any.
cards.why: Red's only counter to its own swaps; he called it frustrating, then kept it and made it cheaper.
cards.short: Round I: 5 buys 3 red members and shuts your cult to swaps.

cards.name: Headhunter
cards.text: On Use, once per game: swap a rival’s member with a shop member that costs as much or more.
cards.bestTurn: Round III: the leader's Patriarch goes to the shop and they get a 10-cost plain member instead; I can buy Patriarch next turn.
cards.topCase: Once a game, deals in round III: the rival loses an ability but gains as much or more cost. About 2 to 4 of swing for 8. Flat.
cards.ideaWhy: Demote's job with a twist that pays the rival.
cards.ties: Same as Demote: blocked by Loyalists, touches the shop row.
cards.coryNotes: Oct 25: "yes" to its name and price.
cards.why: Costs 8 to hand a rival an equal or better member; Demote already does it harder.
cards.short: Round III: send the leader's Patriarch to the shop, then buy it yourself.
cards.risk: Overlaps Demote: both pull a rival's member to the shop.

overlaps: Promote "Swap any member with one in another cult or the shop costing up to 3 more. +3 red." and Demote "Swap any member with one in another cult or the shop costing up to 3 less. +3 red.": the same swap, same round.
Panel "On Use, once per round: promote or demote another of your members." repeats Promote and Demote on a member.
Headhunter "On Use, once per game: swap a rival’s member with a shop member that costs as much or more." and Demote: both pull a rival's member out to the shop.

Foster Parents "Whenever a member joins your cult from a rival’s, +2 followers." and Deprogrammers "Whenever you take a rival’s member out of their cult, they lose 1 follower.": both pay on the same event.
Host "On Recruit: +1 red per 2 members you have. Round Start: +1 red per 2 members you have." and Recruiter "Whenever you recruit a member, +1 red.": both are red income.

Walk-In "Recruit the top member of the pile. Each rival +1 red. +1 red." and Initiation "Recruit a member in the shop costing 10 or less, for free. +1 red.": in round III, Walk-In is a blind, uncapped Initiation.
Seat Filler "Round Start: you may give this to the shop and recruit a shop member costing up to 3 more, for free." and Promote: the same trade up.

Tryout "Use the On Recruit effect of a shop member; it stays in the shop. +2 red." and Green's Sample "Copy the On Recruit of a rival’s member. +1 green.": using another member's On Recruit is Green's job.

Gather "+2 red in round I, +3 in round II, +4 in round III. This turn, if you recruit a member, +1 follower in round I, +2 in round II, +3 in round III.", Magenta's Stash "+2 magenta in round I, +3 in round II, +4 in round III. This turn, if you recruit a member, +1 follower in round I, +2 in round II, +3 in round III." and White's Allowance "+3 white in round I, +4 in round II, +5 in round III. This turn, if you recruit a member, +1 follower in round I, +2 in round II, +3 in round III.": the same card.
notes: Red has five swap cards (Promote, Demote, Panel, Body Snatchers, Headhunter) and one counter, Loyalists. The contest counts members that count as several, so cheap big bodies (Deprogrammers 4 for 5, Loyalists 3 for 5) decide it in round I, more than any card's printed rule. Most pricey members deal only in round III, so Mob, Panel, Body Snatchers, Mentor and Headhunter fire once or not at all. The round III payoff is Initiation plus Patriarch.
storyShort: Red recruits free members and swaps members with the shop and with rivals.
